steps.b: Book a slot or DM us. Any problem, in your own words.
We read up on you first. On the call we name the likely cause and the ways to fix it.
If a project makes sense, you get one short brief: what we’ll do, what you get, and a fixed fee.
Fixes that are light to run: a pricing structure, a tracker, a process your staff can follow.
Questions about what we built? Ask. Linked projects come later, only if you want them.

principles.b: Every consult starts with homework on your business, your street and your competitors.
Bad news included. You’re paying for the honest read, not for comfort.
When cash is tight, we look for savings before anything that costs you more.
What we build is yours and simple to run. No lock-in, no software you have to keep paying for.

faqServices.q: How much does a project cost?
faqServices.a: We quote a fixed fee after the free consult, once we know the scope. Rates are agreed per engagement.

faqServices.q: How long does a project take?
faqServices.a: Most run [two to six] weeks, depending on scope. We agree the timeline in the brief.

faqServices.q: Do I need to prepare anything?
faqServices.a: No. If you have sales records or a rough stock list, they help. We can start without them.

faqServices.q: Will you make our social posts?
faqServices.a: No. We set the strategy: who to reach, what to say and where. Making the content stays with you.

faqContact.a: Yes. We name the likely cause and the directions to fix it. The detailed fix is the paid project, if you want one.
Consults are by video call so they fit around your opening hours.

faqContact.q: What if I don’t know what’s wrong?
faqContact.a: That’s normal. Tell us what you’re seeing. Working back to the cause is our job.

insights.headline: Why does every shop on this street sell the same thing?
insights.lede: Walk down [street] and the racks start to blur. Same brands, same price points, same handwritten tags.
body: When shops source from the same places, they end up competing on the one thing left: price. That is a race the smallest shop rarely wins.
The gap is curation. Customers will pay for a shop that has already done the sorting for them: a clear edit, a reason to come back on a given day, and a story behind the rail.
We walked [n] shops on [street] over [period], logged what each sold and how each priced, and compared it with where they say they source.
## What an owner can do this month
Pick one edit you can own and say it on the shopfront. Price the edit as a set, not item by item. Track which edit sells through fastest and drop the slowest.

insights.headline: Your 1-for-1 is teaching customers to wait.
insights.lede: Run the same deal every Tuesday and Tuesday becomes the only day some regulars show up.
body: Discounts move volume on the day. The cost shows up later, as full-price days get quieter and the deal becomes the price customers expect.

There are better levers. A bundle raises the bill without cutting the headline price. An anchor item makes the main menu look like good value. A discount tied to a slow hour fills the gap without training the whole week.
We compared [n] months of [café] sales on deal days against the days around them, with the owner’s permission.
## What an owner can do this month
Swap one standing discount for a bundle. Keep the price on the board the same and watch the average bill for four weeks.

receipt.title: Deal day check
receipt.finding: The deal moved demand. It didn’t add it.

insights.headline: The salon owner who answers every DM herself.
insights.lede: Bookings, reschedules, price questions, all through one phone. The business grows exactly as fast as she can reply.
body: Most of those messages ask the same five things. Each one takes a minute; together they take the hours that should go to clients or to growing the business.
The fix is unglamorous: a short menu of answers, a booking link that handles the rest, and one rule for what still needs her personally.
We sorted [n] weeks of the owner’s messages by type and timed how long each kind took to close.
## What an owner can do this month
Count your messages for one week by type. Write a saved reply for the top three. Put the booking link in your bio and your auto-reply.

receipt.title: Inbox sort
receipt.finding: Most messages need an answer, not her.
